gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each router costs per Mbps of WireGuard throughput. At GL.iNet's US store prices on 2026-11-08, the Beryl 7 is about $0.12 per WireGuard Mbps and the Beryl AX about $0.33. So the router ChatGPT labelled 'best value' (Beryl AX) costs 2.8× more for each Mbps of VPN speed. No result gives the routers' measured power draw in watts or how long a power bank keeps one running either.
standout_why: I opened racksandwatts.com (Beryl 7 vs Beryl AX, 2026-10-23), stayingconnectedabroad.com (2026-10-12) and itechguides.com (2026-08-11). All three give the maker's WireGuard ceilings, and itechguides and stayingconnectedabroad give prices. None divides price by VPN throughput. None gives a measured power draw: racksandwatts lists only USB-C input ratings, and itechguides only '5V/3A'. None works out runtime on a power bank. Our current page has neither figure. ChatGPT's cited pages (GL.iNet's Beryl 7 and Slate 7 product pages and the MT3000 datasheet) give the raw maker figures but no ratios.
decides: The figures back the Beryl 7 as the pick for a VPN-first shopper and show that 'best value' is the wrong label for the Beryl AX on the number this question is about. The Beryl 7 costs $31.00 more for 800 Mbps more WireGuard ceiling, about 3.9¢ per extra Mbps. The Beryl AX stays the cheaper buy only when the hotel connection is under 300 Mbps, its ceiling. On battery, the Beryl 7 drew 3.7–3.8 W in NASCompares' streaming test. That is about 2.7 h per 10 Wh a power bank delivers, so either router runs for hours on a common power bank. Battery life doesn't split them.
